quotes.text:
A man's life is what his thoughts make of it.
— Marcus Aurelius

Such as are your habitual thoughts, such also will be the character of your mind; for the soul is dyed by the thoughts.
— Marcus Aurelius

If it is not right, do not do it; if it is not true, do not say it.
— Marcus Aurelius

If you are pained by any external thing, it is not this thing that disturbs you, but your own judgement about it. And it is in your power to wipe out this judgement now.
— Marcus Aurelius

Whatever any one does or says, I must be emerald and keep my colour.
— Marcus Aurelius

Loss is nothing else but change, and change is Nature's delight.
— Marcus Aurelius

The best way of avenging yourself is not to become like the wrong-doer.
— Marcus Aurelius

Confine yourself to the present.
— Marcus Aurelius

Adapt yourself to the things with which your lot has been cast, and love sincerely the fellow-creatures with whom destiny has ordained that you shall live.
— Marcus Aurelius

Everything that happens happens as it should, and if you observe carefully, you will find this to be so.
— Marcus Aurelius

If one does not know to which port one is sailing, no wind is favourable.
— Seneca

While we are postponing, life speeds on.
— Seneca

Nothing is ours, except time.
— Seneca

It is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste a great deal of it.
— Seneca

It is quality, not quantity, that matters.
— Seneca

Begin at once to live, and count each separate day as a separate life.
— Seneca

No man ever became wise by chance.
— Seneca

The greatest obstacle to living is expectation, which hangs upon tomorrow and loses today.
— Seneca

Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views which they take of them.
— Epictetus

No man is free who is not master of himself.
— Epictetus

Wealth consists not in having great possessions, but in having few wants.
— Epictetus

First say to yourself what you would be; and then do what you have to do.
— Epictetus

If you would improve, be content to be thought foolish and stupid.
— Epictetus

No great thing is created suddenly, any more than a bunch of grapes or a fig.
— Epictetus

If anyone tells you that a certain person speaks ill of you, do not make excuses about what is said of you, but answer: he was ignorant about my other faults, else he would not have mentioned these alone.
— Epictetus
